record.title: Audio discovery can affect graphical startup
record.method: Original CoreAudio client queries and mediaserverd thread capture
record.observation: Publishing one compatible IOAudio2 output cleared a measured null-device media startup fault. The original client opened and mapped it; mediaserverd reached its event loop.
record.limits: The backend was unbound and playback unsupported. Enumeration and mapped PCM memory are not audible output.

exhibits.title: What the original media client actually returned
exhibits.interpretation: Enumeration and mapping removed a startup dependency. Neither a device ID nor a mapped buffer is evidence of sound.

exhibits.interpretation: These are exact-build interface measurements from the notebook. Timestamp/counter publication and a physical sink need their own acceptance evidence.

excerpts.content:
The private 4A102 kernel analysis identifies an initial 44,100 Hz,
two-channel, 16-bit linear PCM output: 4 bytes per frame, a 65,536-byte
buffer (16,384 frames), and a 512-frame safety offset. The original status
descriptor requests 24 bytes. Its first two 64-bit fields hold completed
frames and a completion timestamp; the third changes on stream startup.
The original completion path advances frames from reported completed bytes.
These facts guide the adapter, but the final callback ABI,

[…]

Its type-0 connection registers
a notification port and maps status memory type 0 (at least 24 bytes) plus
PCM memory type `0x10000000 + stream ID`. Selectors 0 and 1 start and stop
the stream.
